pull_request.body:
## Summary
- Keep a reachable engine attached when its fingerprint RPC is inconclusive, while still replacing positively mismatched builds.
- Debounce unreachable supervision ticks and emit production logs that identify the liveness source and restart evidence.
- Add regression coverage for unresponsive fingerprint RPCs and consecutive-failure restart scheduling.

## Validation
- `bazel build //tools/boss/app-macos:boss_mac_app_lib //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3`
- `bazel test //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3`
- `bazel build //tools/boss/app-macos:Boss //tools/boss/installer:release`
- `checkleft run`

item.text: The comparison contains four changed files. The key distinction is between a missing fingerprint and a confirmed mismatch: only the latter now triggers replacement. I’m also checking what the liveness signal measures so the guide separates reachability from proof that the engine is healthy.

load(
    "//tools/boss/engine/core:engine_binary.bzl",
    "ENGINE_BINARY_BAZEL_OUTPUT_FRAGMENT",
    "ENGINE_BINARY_BAZEL_RUN_COMMAND",
    "ENGINE_BINARY_BUNDLE_FRAGMENT",
    "ENGINE_BINARY_NAME",
    "ENGINE_BINARY_TARGET",
)
load("//tools/boss/installer:pkg.bzl", "boss_short_version_plist")
load("//tools/test-sandbox:defs.bzl", "XCODE_TEST_ENV")

config_setting(
    name = "coverage_enabled",
    values = {"collect_code_coverage": "true"},
)

_COVERAGE_LINKOPTS = select({
    ":coverage_enabled": ["-fprofile-instr-generate"],
    "//conditions:default": [],
})

_ENGINE_BINARY_SWIFT_SOURCE = """enum BossEngineBinary {
    static let executableName = \"%s\"
    static let bazelRunCommand = \"%s\"
    static let bazelOutputPathFragment = \"%s\"
    static let bundlePathFragment = \"%s\"
}
""" % (
    ENGINE_BINARY_NAME,
    ENGINE_BINARY_BAZEL_RUN_COMMAND,
    ENGINE_BINARY_BAZEL_OUTPUT_FRAGMENT,
    ENGINE_BINARY_BUNDLE_FRAGMENT,
)

package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:private"])

exports_files([
    "Package.resolved",
    "Package.swift",
    "ghosttykit.BUILD",
])

swift_library(
    name = "boss_mac_app_lib",
    # CrashWatchdog is excluded so it is only ever compiled as its own module
    # (matching Package.swift's `exclude:`); leaving it in the glob would give
    # the app a second, shadowing copy of the type it imports.
    #
    # Sources/EngineBinaryName.swift is excluded too: it's a checked-in copy
    # of the genrule output below, kept in the tree only so SwiftPM/Xcode
    # (which never see bazel genrules) can compile it. Bazel itself keeps
    # compiling the genrule's output as the single source of truth; the
    # checked-in copy is verified byte-identical to it by
    # :engine_binary_name_swift_up_to_date_test.
    srcs = glob(
        ["Sources/**/*.swift"],
        exclude = [
            "Sources/CrashWatchdog/**/*.swift",
            "Sources/EngineBinaryName.swift",
        ],
    ) + [":engine_binary_name_swift"],
    copts = [
        # Mirror the swiftSettings define in Package.swift so @inlinable
        # Textual APIs (e.g. .textual.textSelection) expand correctly here.
        "-DTEXTUAL_ENABLE_TEXT_SELECTION",
        # Match Package.swift's `swift-tools-version: 6.2`. Without this,
        # bazel compiles under the rules_swift default (Swift 5 mode) and
        # silently skips the strict-concurrency diagnostics that
        # `swift run` would fire. CI then passes on changes that break
        # the dev workflow — see #601 (LogViewer.swift global formatter)
        # for a recent example.
        "-swift-version",
        "6",
        "-strict-concurrency=complete",
    ],
    module_name = "Boss",
    deps = [
        "//tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/CrashWatchdog",
        "//tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/UpdateCore",
        "@ghostty_kit//:GhosttyKit",
        "@swiftpkg_textual//:Textual",
    ],
)

genrule(
    name = "engine_binary_name_swift",
    outs = ["EngineBinaryName.swift"],
    cmd = "cat > $@ <<'EOF'\n%sEOF" % _ENGINE_BINARY_SWIFT_SOURCE,
    visibility = ["//visibility:private"],
)

# Guards the checked-in Sources/EngineBinaryName.swift (needed so
# SwiftPM/Xcode builds resolve `BossEngineBinary` — they never see bazel
# genrules) against drifting from the genrule above, which stays the single
# source of truth for bazel builds. Fails the moment the two disagree, e.g.
# because ENGINE_BINARY_NAME or another engine_binary.bzl constant changed
# without the checked-in copy being regenerated.
sh_test(
    name = "engine_binary_name_swift_up_to_date_test",
    srcs = ["engine_binary_name_swift_up_to_date_test.sh"],
    args = [
        "$(location Sources/EngineBinaryName.swift)",
        "$(location :engine_binary_name_swift)",
    ],
    data = [
        "Sources/EngineBinaryName.swift",
        ":engine_binary_name_swift",
    ],
)

# BossTests is sharded across four independent macos_unit_test targets so
# each one fits comfortably inside the "small" (60s) timeout as the suite
# grows (see CI timeout in exec_18bf0a6008fc0cc0_170). rules_apple's default
# macos test runner (apple/testing/default_runner) does not implement Bazel's
# native shard_count sharding protocol (no TEST_SHARD_INDEX/TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS
# handling), so `shard_count` on a single macos_unit_test is a no-op here —
# splitting into separate targets is the mechanism that actually parallelizes
# test execution for this rule.
#
# CommentsTests.swift + TranscriptViewTests.swift are split into their own
# shard because CommentLayerTests alone accounts for ~85% of total XCTest
# runtime (~12.8s of ~14.9s measured locally); bundling it with anything else
# risks that shard alone approaching the timeout. The remaining files are
# split into three buckets balanced by source line count.
#
# Shard3 is a catch-all glob rather than a fourth hand-listed file set: the
# first three shards' file lists are named below and fed into both their own
# srcs and shard3's glob exclude, so those two views of the same lists can
# never drift apart. Any new file added under Tests/BossTests/ therefore
# automatically lands in shard3 and runs, instead of silently being skipped
# by every shard (a false green) because no one remembered to hand-list it.
_COMMENTS_TRANSCRIPT_SHARD_SRCS = [
    "Tests/BossTests/CommentsTests.swift",
    "Tests/BossTests/TranscriptViewTests.swift",
]

_SHARD1_SRCS = [
    "Tests/BossTests/APIKeyStoreTests.swift",
    "Tests/BossTests/ApplyAttentionGroupsListTests.swift",
    "Tests/BossTests/AttachmentAffordanceTests.swift",

    "Tests/BossTests/ProductCreateFormCopyTests.swift",

]

macos_unit_test(

# TestSourcesDoNotCallRealOpenerTests.swift (which lands in this shard via the
# glob below) scans all BossTests sources for banned real-OS-opener APIs. Under
# `swift test`/Xcode it does that scan at test *runtime* using `#filePath`, but
# `bazel test` compiles Swift with `-file-prefix-pwd-is-dot`, which rewrites
# `#filePath` to a build-relative path that doesn't match the runtime cwd —
# scanning at runtime under bazel silently finds nothing. So under bazel we
# instead run the same scan as a build action, over the real `srcs` Bazel
# resolved, and bake the result into a generated Swift file the test asserts
# against (selected via the BOSS_BAZEL_TEST_BUILD compile condition below).
genrule(
    name = "generate_real_opener_scan",
    srcs = glob(
        ["Tests/BossTests/**/*.swift"],
        exclude = ["Tests/BossTests/TestSourcesDoNotCallRealOpenerTests.swift"],
    ),
    outs = ["GeneratedRealOpenerScanResult.swift"],
    cmd = "bash $(location Tests/BossTests/scan_for_real_openers.sh) $(SRCS) > $@",
    tools = ["Tests/BossTests/scan_for_real_openers.sh"],
)

swift_library(
    name = "boss_mac_app_tests_shard3_lib",
    testonly = True,
    srcs = glob(
        ["Tests/BossTests/**/*.swift"],
        exclude = _COMMENTS_TRANSCRIPT_SHARD_SRCS + _SHARD1_SRCS + _SHARD2_SRCS,
    ) + [":generate_real_opener_scan"],
    copts = [
        "-DTEXTUAL_ENABLE_TEXT_SELECTION",
        "-DBOSS_BAZEL_TEST_BUILD",
    ],
    linkopts = _COVERAGE_LINKOPTS,
    module_name = "BossTestsShard3",
    deps = [":boss_mac_app_lib"],
)

# Stamps CFBundleShortVersionString (full version, e.g. "1.0.4-dev-f3be785") and
# CFBundleVersion (numeric-only, e.g. "1.0.4") from workspace-status.sh stable keys.
# Both keys are in one plist to ensure our values are the final word — using
# apple_bundle_version alongside infoplists caused apple_bundle_version's version
# provider to be merged after infoplists, silently overriding CFBundleShortVersionString.
boss_short_version_plist(
    name = "boss_version_plist",
    out = "BossVersion.plist",
    visibility = ["//visibility:private"],
)

macos_application(
    name = "Boss",
    # Bundle the engine and the Boss CLIs into Contents/Resources/bin/ so that
    # a single `bazel build //tools/boss/app-macos:Boss` produces a fully
    # self-contained .app (design doc Q3 on-disk layout, Q4 Phase 1).
    # cube is bundled so the engine can find it even when the macOS GUI launchd
    # PATH excludes the user's shell PATH (see config.rs resolve_cube_command).
    # Workers run inside Ghostty terminal panes and inherit the user's shell PATH,
    # so they continue to resolve cube (and jj, gh, claude, etc.) from PATH.
    additional_contents = {
        ENGINE_BINARY_TARGET: "Resources/bin",
        "//tools/boss/cli:boss": "Resources/bin",
        "//tools/boss/bossctl:bossctl": "Resources/bin",
        "//tools/boss/event-shim:boss-event": "Resources/bin",
        "//tools/cube:cube": "Resources/bin",
        "//tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Resources/TrekIcons:trek_icons": "Resources/TrekIcons",
        # relaunch-helper.sh: the detached swap/relaunch watchdog the app spawns
        # after UpdateInstaller (UpdateCore) stages the new bundle in-process.
        # Bundled at Resources/ top level so the app resolves it with
        # Bundle.main.url(forResource: "relaunch-helper", withExtension: "sh").
        "//tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Resources/RelaunchHelper:relaunch_helper": "Resources",
    },
    bundle_id = "dev.spinyfin.bossmacapp",
    infoplists = [
        "Info.plist",
        ":boss_version_plist",
    ],
    minimum_os_version = "15.0",
    visibility = ["//tools/boss/installer:__pkg__"],
    deps = [":boss_mac_app_lib"],
)
